html:
The Darkinyung are an Aboriginal Australian people of New South Wales, in the sandstone country north of the Hawkesbury River, between Sydney and the Hunter Valley. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their land of ridges, gorges and creeks, around the Macdonald River and Wollombi, holds many rock engravings and painted shelters. Little is recorded in detail of their history. Neighbours on the map include the Wonnarua, the Guringai, the Awabakal and the Dharug. The Great North Road, built by convicts from 1826, crossed their land to link Sydney with the Hunter. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
